doom.driver: Vulnerability giving attackers full control of Macs is under active exploitation. Screen-sharing bug lets remote hackers log in without a password.
doom.blurb: YOUR MAC. THEIR SCREEN. NO PASSWORD REQUIRED.
doom.summary: A zero-click Mac screen-sharing vulnerability is actively being weaponized in the wild, letting remote attackers waltz into your machine without so much as a knock. Coming hot on the heels of Iranian water infrastructure hacks and the government outsourcing its own cyber offense, the theme of this week is clearly 'everyone can hack everything now.' Meanwhile OpenAI and Anthropic are in a price war to make AI cheaper — which will definitely not make any of this worse.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: OpenAI and Anthropic slashing prices in a race to the bottom as Chinese rivals gain ground — democratizing powerful models faster than guardrails can keep up.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: France's top court blocked a social media ban for under-15s on free speech grounds, illustrating how courts keep outrunning tech policy globally.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Israeli strikes intensify in Lebanon, West Bank raids continue, South Korea proposes Korean War end talks, and Taiwan finally passed its delayed defence budget — several slow-burn fronts simultaneously warming.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Alibaba dropped Qwen3.8-27B to Hacker News fanfare — the open-source capability march continues regardless of what the big labs decide to restrict.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A 7.7-magnitude earthquake in Indonesia kills at least 38, 'unprecedented' flooding strands thousands in Japan — natural disaster load unusually high for a single weekend.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — interior scene, we are inside a dim Dutch apartment in Amsterdam looking outward through a rain-streaked window toward a canal-flanked brick street, deep winter night, wet cobblestones reflecting smoldering orange sodium streetlamps below a deep navy sky — the room itself is the story: a wooden desk pushed against the window holds a Mac laptop, lid open, screen casting cold blue-white light upward onto the ceiling, the display showing a cursor drifting slowly across the desktop with no hand touching the trackpad, the chair pushed back and empty, a ceramic mug steaming gently beside an absent owner's coat draped over the chair back — on the screen's glow we can see the faint ghost of System Settings open, a toggle visibly switched on — the walls of the apartment are steeped in heavy shadow, smoldering orange from the streetlights bleeding through the rain-wet glass cutting diagonal warm slashes across dark floorboards, the warmth feeling deeply wrong against the cold machine's unauthorized activity — outside through the window a neighbor's lit window shows a silhouette seated calmly at their own desk, unaware, the canal below still and black — the Mac's fan grille glows faintly hot amber, CPU working hard in the dark for someone far away.

dawn.driver: In Australia, a home battery boom has helped cut wholesale power prices.
dawn.blurb: BATTERIES ARE WINNING THE ENERGY WAR
dawn.summary: While headlines fill with earthquakes, conflict, and cyber threats, Australia is quietly demonstrating that the clean energy transition works — and saves money. A boom in home battery installations has meaningfully cut wholesale electricity prices, proving that distributed, citizen-powered energy storage is a real economic force, not just an idealist's dream. On a day when pDoom sits at 35.4%, this is the kind of structural, unglamorous progress that actually bends the long arc of history toward resilience.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Australia's home battery boom cutting wholesale power prices shows clean energy transition delivering tangible, market-measurable results at scale.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: JWST's discovery of a 'black hole star' 100 billion times brighter than a star and new cosmic mapping of three million spectra expand humanity's grasp of the universe.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: South Korea's president formally proposed talks with North Korea to end the Korean War, a rare and significant diplomatic gesture across one of the world's most frozen conflicts.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: A Washington state community rallied together to celebrate and thank firefighters after devastating wildfires, demonstrating resilience and mutual care in the face of disaster.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: American Samoa's stunning upset of the U.S. flag football team — ending a 14-year streak — is a joyful reminder that small nations can punch far above their weight on the world stage.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Wide aerial view looking down at a 45-degree angle, vast Australian suburban streetscape dominates the frame, golden-hour amber light raking long honeyed shadows across a dense grid of terracotta-roofed homes stretching to the horizon, every rooftop visible from above — roughly one in three glittering with deep blue-black solar panels catching the last hard afternoon sun like beetle wings, the rest bare by contrast, making the adoption pattern immediately readable as a geometric patchwork across the neighborhood. Far below, tiny figures of residents stand in driveways looking up, ant-sized, dwarfed by the scale of the landscape. The second-order effect dominates: on the far edge of the composition, a row of massive electricity transmission pylons and high-voltage lines recedes into the background, their indicator lights dark and idle, load visibly shed, the infrastructure quietly redundant against the humming self-sufficiency of the suburb ahead of it. Sleek white rectangular home battery units dot exterior walls across dozens of homes, visible as small bright rectangles from above. A single electric vehicle in a driveway shows a glowing green charge light. Color palette is deep solar gold, warm teal sky, electric blue panels, clean white battery units, long amber shadows burning across cream weatherboard. Radiant, triumphant, communal, quietly revolutionary.
